About

I am a spatial epidemiologist with over 15 years in public health intelligence and research. I use maps, travel-time models and routine health data to find gaps in access to care, especially for mothers and children.

  • Lecturer in Geographies of Health at UCL’s Department of Geography.
  • Lead of the UCL Geographies of Health research cluster.
  • Former Senior Research Fellow with WorldPop, University of Southampton.
  • Public Health Officer with the Ghana Health Service, then monitoring and evaluation lead at Good Neighbors Ghana.
Regions
Ghana, Nigeria and the UK
Recognition
ESRC Celebrating Impact Prize 2022, runner-up for Early Career Impact

Research themes

Access to care travel time

How far people live from care, and how distance and quality shape whether they use it.

Maternal and child health EmONC

Where women give birth, who misses care, and how to bring quality services closer.

Climate and health flooding

How floods and other climate shocks disrupt health services and health outcomes.

Routine health data DHIMS

Turning data that health systems already collect into evidence for planning.
